döner kebab.guidance: Spiced meat, salad and garlic sauce suit fresh rosé, juicy Grenache or dry bubbles. With hot chile sauce, favor a lighter, lower-alcohol bottle.
döner kebab.basis: Editorial style match informed by the reference; regional profiles are not individual bottle recommendations.

carne asada.guidance: Charred beef suits fruit-led reds with enough structure for the meat. Choose a fresher, less alcoholic bottle when salsa brings substantial heat.

tacos al pastor.guidance: Chile-marinated pork and pineapple suit fresh, savory reds or a bright dry Riesling. Very hot salsa calls for a gentler, off-dry option.
tacos al pastor.basis: Editorial style match informed by the reference; regional profiles are not individual bottle recommendations.

tacos de cochinita pibil.guidance: Citrus-marinated pork and achiote favor fresh acidity and some texture. Fresh Chenin Blanc or rosé can balance the citrus and pork richness; habanero salsa changes the match.

sushi and nigiri.guidance: For delicate fish and vinegared rice, choose fresh acidity and restrained tannin. Rich sauces and generous wasabi can shift the pairing.

spicy sushi rolls.guidance: For chile or spicy mayonnaise, look for an off-dry bottle with moderate alcohol. Check the producer: these regional profiles also include dry examples.

phở bò.guidance: Aromatic beef broth suits dry bubbles or a delicate Pinot Noir. Keep tannin restrained, and adjust for added hoisin or chile.

shoyu ramen.guidance: Soy and dashi favor a delicate, savory Pinot Noir; dry sparkling wine is a refreshing alternative. Broth style matters more than the noodles.

tonkotsu ramen.guidance: Rich pork-bone broth can take a structured savory red; dry bubbles offer a fresher contrast. Heavy chile additions favor gentler alcohol and tannin.

miso ramen.guidance: Fermented miso and savory broth suit earthy Pinot Noir or dry sparkling wine. For spicy miso, consider a little sweetness instead.
miso ramen.basis: Editorial style match informed by the reference; regional profiles are not individual bottle recommendations.

falafel.guidance: Herbs, chickpeas and a crisp fried crust favor bright whites, dry bubbles or fresh rosé. Tahini adds richness; hot sauce changes the balance.

hummus.guidance: Lemon, tahini and creamy chickpeas suit fresh acidity. These crisp styles provide contrast without covering the sesame and garlic.

vietnamese summer rolls.guidance: Fresh herbs and rice-paper rolls suit crisp Riesling or Sauvignon Blanc. A sweet peanut dip may call for a slightly off-dry bottle.

bánh xèo.guidance: A crisp savory pancake suits fresh dry sparkling wine. Choose a dry bottling and account for the sweetness or chile in the dipping sauce.

pepperoni pizza.guidance: Tomato, cured meat and melted cheese suit a fresh savory red. For very hot pepperoni, keep alcohol moderate.

mushroom pizza.guidance: Mushroom umami and cheese suit earthy reds. Favor mature Nebbiolo with softened tannins or a gentler Pinot Noir.

white pizza.guidance: Without tomato, cheese and creamy toppings favor Chardonnay or a delicate Pinot Noir. Garlic and herbs influence the final match.

fried chicken.guidance: For a salty crisp crust, dry sparkling wine brings acidity and bubbles. Sweet glazes or substantial chile call for a different balance.

buffalo wings.guidance: Hot sauce and butter favor moderate alcohol, bright acidity and a little sweetness. Choose an off-dry bottling, especially with a hot sauce.
